title: DIAMETER: remove tree inside grouped AVP
description:
Remove additional tree of all child AVP inside grouped AVP
and made this item as generated.

[Example file](/uploads/35d2ce8b5f3bb00309f0e54c77177cf0/example.pcap)

Before
```
Subscription-Id
    AVP Code: 443 Subscription-Id
    AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
    AVP Length: 40
    Subscription-Id
        Subscription-Id-Type: END_USER_E164 (0)
        Subscription-Id-Data: 79001234567

```


After
```
Subscription-Id
    AVP Code: 443 Subscription-Id
    AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
    AVP Length: 40
    [Subscription-Id]
    Subscription-Id-Type: END_USER_E164 (0)
    Subscription-Id-Data: 79001234567

```

notes.body:
added 22 commits
  • 18a1a0a9...17d660e7 - 21 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • ba1fc058 - DIAMETER: remove tree inside grouped AVP
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/22531/diffs?diff_id=1584499751&start_sha=18a1a0a9cc574d7e731e3ac960400f70aa340a2c)

I think the tree member of diam_ctx_t struct gives you access to the top tree where yopu can add:

`Subscription-Id: END_USER_E164 (0) 79001234567`

`Wouldn't that work better?`

Sorry item in this struct:

`diam_sub_dis_t`

My final idea is
```
Subscription-Id: MSISDN=79001234567
    AVP Code: 443 Subscription-Id
    AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
    AVP Length: 40
    [Subscription-Id] // used only for filter "diameter.Subscription-Id" and no need add any info
    Subscription-Id-Type: END_USER_E164 (0)
    Subscription-Id-Data: 79001234567
```

Remove tree for child items will improve visual representation
Not sure how it will look for other grouped avp:s, maybe many avps and nested.

Groped AVP has another grouped AVP as child
```
Multiple-Services-Credit-Control: RG=12345, RC=2001 \\ Parent grouped AVP
    AVP Code: 456 Multiple-Services-Credit-Control
    AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
    AVP Length: 84
    [Multiple-Services-Credit-Control]
    Rating-Group: 12345
        AVP Code: 432 Rating-Group
        AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
        AVP Length: 12
        Rating-Group: 12345
    Result-Code: DIAMETER_SUCCESS (2001)
    Granted-Service-Unit: Total-Octets=219715200 \\ Nested grouped AVP
        AVP Code: 431 Granted-Service-Unit
        AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
        AVP Length: 24
        [Granted-Service-Unit]
        CC-Total-Octets: 219715200
            AVP Code: 421 CC-Total-Octets
            AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
            AVP Length: 16
            CC-Total-Octets: 219715200
    Validity-Time: 3600
    Volume-Quota-Threshold: 1024000
```
May be it will better create new merge request which will include this one and !22470 [Draft: DIAMETER: append information to grouped AVP]
You can also just use this MR for the functionality of both (just push it all to the same branch name), just to have the history of changes.
Added second commit  !22470 [Draft: DIAMETER: append information to grouped AVP]

Why not removed this also? After looking into these I feel like the value presented THREE times is a bit too much

```
Subscription-Id
    AVP Code: 443 Subscription-Id
    AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
    AVP Length: 40
    Subscription-Id
        Subscription-Id-Type: END_USER_E164 (0)
        Subscription-Id-Data: 1707818047
```

to

```
Subscription-Id
    AVP Code: 443 Subscription-Id
    AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
    AVP Length: 40
    Subscription-Id-Type: END_USER_E164 (0)
    Subscription-Id-Data: 1707818047
```

Can not delete as these items are used for different filteres.

At present moment items have filters
```
Subscription-Id // -> diameter.avp
    AVP Code: 443 Subscription-Id
    AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
    AVP Length: 40
    Subscription-Id // -> diameter.Subscription-Id
        Subscription-Id-Type: END_USER_E164 (0)
        Subscription-Id-Data: 79001234567
```

After 
```
Subscription-Id // -> diameter.avp
    AVP Code: 443 Subscription-Id
    AVP Flags: 0x40, Mandatory: Set
    AVP Length: 40
    [Subscription-Id] // -> diameter.Subscription-Id
    Subscription-Id-Type: END_USER_E164 (0)
    Subscription-Id-Data: 79001234567
```

We can't remove filters like `diameter.Subscription-Id`. May be replace item with filter `diameter.avp` by item with filter `diameter.Subscription-Id` (use `diameter.Subscription-Id` as parent tree)?
Yes, filtering on a tree value doesn't sound correct. The correct filter to me would be "diameter.avp.code == 443"

I'm not talking about "correctness" of fillters. Two items have the same text but different purposes. We can't replace/remove item `Subscription-Id [diameter.avp]` as it used to hold all sub elements: `AVP-Code, Flags ...` and has type `FT_BYTES`. For non-grouped AVP this is not problem as they have separate item (with exact filter, like diameter.Session-Id ) of exact type `FT_UINT32, FT_STRING, ...` but grouped AVP has item (like diameter.Subscription-Id)  of type FT_BYTES which also is used as tree for child items.

Now it's necessary expand two trees to view child items, but I suggest remove tree for child items. But we need keep this item. That is why I maked it as generated to have filteres like `diameter.Subscription-Id`

commits_data.message:
DIAMETER: append information to grouped AVP

Now grouped AVPs have no any information in tree and it's necessary to expand each item to get details.
This change allows child AVPs append information to parent AVP.
